claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can initially exist fully in a high-temperature BCC state.
The stability of the high-temperature BCC phase is governed by a balance between the thermodynamic driving force for decomposition and kinetic hindrance from Al-induced local chemical ordering.
Al-induced local chemical ordering increases the energetic barrier for nucleation of a competing phase.
FCC is a possible competing phase that can nucleate from the BCC state.
Thermodynamic instability becomes more significant at lower temperatures.
Kinetic hindrance delays transformation even when the thermodynamic instability is significant.
Temperatures of approximately 600–800°C are below or span the relevant BCC stability limit or transformation regime for this alloy.
Al atoms preferentially induce short-range order within the BCC matrix.
Al-induced short-range order alters interatomic bonding.
The ordered regions raise the barrier to nucleation and growth of the thermodynamically favored phase upon cooling.
Within the proposed aging regime, the rate of BCC-to-FCC transformation or secondary-phase emergence will increase as aging temperature decreases.
Transformation will remain slower than it would be in the absence of kinetic barriers.
Samples receiving minimal aging will retain the BCC phase.
A sample quenched from the high-temperature BCC state without aging will show no significant transformation.
The proposed mechanism applies where diffusion is slow enough for Al-induced ordering to dominate transformation kinetics.
At very high temperatures, rapid diffusion prevents the proposed ordering-controlled interplay from governing phase stability.
At very low temperatures, transformation is suppressed entirely.
